newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - June 9.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - June 9.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends ***********************************************
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

AMSTERDAM - Global advertising agencies, recently hit by tumultuous changes in ownership, must brace themselves for more big shake-ups, says Martin Sorrell, group chief executive of WPP Group Plc, the world's largest advertising and marketing services group.
JAKARTA - Growing consumer demand is expected to boost advertising spending in Indonesia to almost five trillion rupiah ($2.06 billion) this year, the Jakarta Post newspaper reports.

ST PETERSBURG - President Boris Yeltsin says he is coming round to the idea of a ban on foreign-language advertisments, saying it is time to promote Russian and stem the tide of alien tongues on Moscow's streets.

PARIS - French advertising agency Euro RSCG Worldwide says it has won the accounts to advertise Sara Lee Corp brands Playtex and Wonderbra in Europe. New advertisements will begin appearing in the second half of this year.

LONDON - C&A, the retail clothing chain, says it will sponsor a second consecutive year MTV Europe's "Turned on Europe" programme. "By extending our relationship with MTV Europe, C&A is underlining its commitment to and focus on the youth market," Jaap Bosman, national advertising director of C&A, says.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

SINGAPORE - Asian print and broadcast media lag behind their Western counterparts, although quality media are not vital for doing business in the region, a report from the Hong Kong-based Political and Economic Risk Consultancy Ltd says. China was regarded the toughest of the markets covered due to censorship and overall quality of local print and broadcast news.
WALLDORF - News channel CNN launches its first German-language service in Germany's most populous state, North Rhine-Westphalia.

JOHANNESBURG - South African publishing firm Times Media Ltd is set to post healthy year earnings growth next week boosted by a strong performance from its core print operations, analysts say. The firm, which publishes Business day, The Financial Mail and the Sunday Times, has benefitted from a boom in advertising revenue as the publishing world expands in post-apartheid South Africa.
BONN - Deutsche Telekom AG plans to charge pay-TV stations 90 million marks ($52 million) for inclusion in its cable network, 30 times to current price, reports news magazine Der Spiegel.
WELLINGTON - Television New Zealand is to close its five regional channels and the broadcast frequency is to be used for a new youth-oriented station, a company spokesman says.

MUNICH - Media giant Bertelsmann forms strategic alliance with information service Reed Elsevier Deutschland to provide online data on the transportation industry. The companies plan to integrate their marketing of internet services, the Bertlesmann industry information division says.
LONDON - Shares in Flextech Plc fell after a report in the Sunday Times newspaper highlighted investor doubts over the cable and satellite television company's strategy, dealers say.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:
LONDON - British Airways Plc says it's launching a 60 million pounds ($97.5 million) overhaul of its livery and corporate identity, with a series of events across the world.
LONDON - British supermarket group Tesco Plc says it is launching a weekly prize draw using its ClubCard loyalty card with offers including a year's free shopping.
BEIJING - Tough new Chinese regulations on importing compact disc production lines are introduced to try to curb widespread copyright piracy, the China Daily says.

SEOUL - The powerful Samsung Group is testing the waters for a potential takeover of South Korea's second-largest carmaker Kia Motors, by leaking an internal report recommending restructuring of the overcrowded industry, analysts say.
LONDON - All foods which may contain genetically modified (GM) ingredients must be labelled clearly to give consumers a real choice in what they buy, British Food Safety Minister Jeff Rooker says.

MODENA, Italy - Car maker Ferrari held a party to celebrate its 50th anniversary, but seven ferrari owners enthusiasts left the party empty-handed after thieves sped off with their prized sports cars.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

LONDON - Help is at hand for chocoholics - a scented, adhesive patch has been launched to stop people from craving chocolate. The small, blue, square patch is saturated with the aroma of a tropical orchid which the manufacturers say can have an almost immediate effect in diminishing the desire for weight-inducing chocolate, biscuits and cakes when worn on the hand, wrist or on the chest.
BEIJING - China's auto industry will begin installing catalytic converters in cars in 2000 in a bid to clean up the air in one of the world's most polluted countries.

HAVANA - In Havana, the stars-and-stripes are officially a fashion "no no". Cuba's official Union of Young Communists citing the threat of "mental colonization", is waging a campaign to persuade young Cubans not to sport clothes bearing the flag of the United States, a Cuban newspaper reports.

HONG KONG - A new-generation of Asian white-collar professionals runs boom-time Hong Kong. These "Chyuppies" (Chinese, young, upwardly mobile persons) wear smart designer clothes and collect glitzy brand-name consumer goods and will be a tough nut for China to crack if it abandons a pledged "hands off" attitude, say Hong Kong experts.

MOSCOW - Men in Russia are less likely to reach the age of 60 than they were 100 years ago, official statistics say. Accidents and poisoning by poor quality alcoholic drinks are the two leading killers of men aged between 16 and 60.
